data.name: Helm v4.3.2
data.body:
Helm v4.3.2 is a patch release. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

The community keeps growing, and we'd love to see you there!

- Join the discussion in [Kubernetes Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com):
  -  for questions and just to hang out
  -  for discussing PRs, code, and bugs
- Hang out at the Public Developer Call: Thursday, 9:30 Pacific via [Zoom](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meeting/91295593969?password=17825db5-c698-44cc-9f00-ef1f61f5d3fb)
- Test, debug, and contribute charts: [ArtifactHub/packages](https://artifacthub.io/packages/search?kind=0)

## Notable Changes

- docs(cmd): correct list --max and HELM_COLOR help text #32807 by @ZainnQureshii
- fix(registry): always return a transport Helm can configure #32684 by @ump45nose

## Installation and Upgrading

Download Helm v4.3.2. The common platform binaries are here:

- [MacOS amd64](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.2-darwin-amd64.tar.gz) ([checksum](https://get.helm.sh/helm-v4.3.2-darwin-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum) / 9e0068e9ae18c441d27388190ee7f53ae65eba44bfe910b40bdac44c4b51fa71)

The [Quickstart Guide](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/quickstart/) will get you going from there. For **upgrade instructions** or detailed installation notes, check the [install guide](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/). You can also use a [script to install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-4) on any system with `bash`.

## What's Next

- 4.3.2 is the next patch releases scheduled for November 11, 2026
- 4.4.0 is the next minor release scheduled for January 13, 2027. There will be no further Helm 3 minor releases (see https://helm.sh/blog/helm-v3-end-of-life)

data.name: pack v0.40.11
data.body:
## Prerequisites

- A container runtime such as [Docker](https://www.docker.com/get-started) or [podman](https://podman.io/get-started) must be available to execute builds.

## Install

For instructions on installing `pack`, see our [installation docs](https://buildpacks.io/docs/tools/pack/cli/install/).

## Run

Run the command `pack`.

You should see the following output

```text
CLI for building apps using Cloud Native Buildpacks

Usage:
  pack [command]

Available Commands:
  build                 Generate app image from source code
  builder               Interact with builders
  buildpack             Interact with buildpacks
  extension             Interact with extensions
  config                Interact with your local pack config file
  inspect               Show information about a built app image
  stack                 (deprecated) Interact with stacks
  rebase                Rebase app image with latest run image
  sbom                  Interact with SBoM
  completion            Outputs completion script location
  report                Display useful information for reporting an issue
  version               Show current 'pack' version
  help                  Help about any command

Flags:
      --force-color   Force color output
  -h, --help          Help for 'pack'
      --no-color      Disable color output
  -q, --quiet         Show less output
      --timestamps    Enable timestamps in output
  -v, --verbose       Show more output
      --version       Show current 'pack' version

Use "pack [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## Info

Builders created with this release of the pack CLI contain [lifecycle v0.21.29](https://github.com/buildpack/lifecycle/releases/tag/v0.21.29) by default.

## Changelog

### Features

* Adding resolute builder to trusted builders (#2739 by @pacostas)
* test: only assert the last line of quiet-mode local build output (#2730 by @Pranav-IIITM)
* deps: bump the default lifecycle to 0.21.29 (#2723 by @jjbustamante)
* chore: drop kaniko dependency (#2677 by @mzihlmann)
* fix: include CA certificates in the pack base image (#2609 by @officialasishkumar)

## Contributors

We'd like to acknowledge that this release wouldn't be as good without the help of the following amazing contributors:

@Pranav-IIITM, @jjbustamante, @mzihlmann, @officialasishkumar, @pacostas

data.name: v1.22.4
data.body:
This is a fix release for a vulnerability (CVE-2026-97054) in Go's HTTP/1 server:

https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM

> net/http: HTTP/1 server crash due to MaxBytesReader header race
>
> For HTTP/1 servers, when MaxBytesReader's limit is exceeded,
> "Connection: close" header is automatically set without synchronization,
> which might race with another header being set explicitly in the server
> handler. As a result, an HTTP/1 server that utilizes MaxBytesReader or
> MaxBytesHandler can crash due to runtime panic if its handler reads the
> request body concurrently with writing the response header.
>
> Thanks to Jakub Ciolek (https://ciolek.dev) for reporting this issue.
>
> This is CVE-2026-97054 and Go issue https://go.dev/issue/82563.

Note that our security guidance includes not running OPA with its interfaces exposed to adversarial actors, like the public internet. This is fixed regardless, if only to avoid too many spurious vulnerability checker reports.

Also note that if you build your OPA binaries yourself, this patch release does not apply to you, as you control the version of Go that's used. This patch release affects the published binaries and docker images of OPA.

data.name: v0.14.4
data.body:
### Changed

- Lowering `[auth] ACTIVATE_CODE_LIVES` or `[auth] RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES` now also shortens the lifetime of activation, email confirmation, and password reset links already sent. [#8478](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8478)

### Fixed

- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, a user creating a repository with initial files or initializing its labels could read files on the server, including the configuration file. [#8488](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8488) - [GHSA-fv2v-vwmj-j74p](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-fv2v-vwmj-j74p)
- _Security:_ Referencing an issue in a commit message added a comment to it even when the pusher could not access its repository, letting anyone post into issues of private repositories. [#8486](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8486) - [GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v)
- _Security:_ Viewing an Org-mode file could show the contents of arbitrary files on the server, including the configuration file. [#8484](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8484) - [GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365)
- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, an authenticated user with write access could still write files into a repository's `.git` directory through other names for it, leading to code execution on the server. [#8483](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8483) - [GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq)
- _Security:_ A username containing HTML, which could come from an external login source such as LDAP, was rendered as markup on issue and pull request pages and in the dashboard issue and pull request lists. [#8482](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8482) - [GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9)
- _Security:_ Webhooks, repository migrations, and mirrors could reach services on the Gogs host through the IPv6 address `[::]`, bypassing the local network restriction. [#8481](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8481) - [GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q)
- _Security:_ Any signed-in user who knew the UUID of an attachment in another repository, including a private one, could move it to their own issue, comment, or release to download it, in some cases removing it from the original. [#8480](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8480) - [GHSA-p92p-7887-3g33](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-p92p-7887-3g33)
- _Security:_ A password reset link could be used to sign in as the user without their password or two-factor authentication. Activation, email confirmation, and password reset links sent before upgrading no longer work. [#8472](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8472) - [GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm)
- _Security:_ Accounts with login prohibited or not activated kept repository access through access tokens, passwords, and SSH keys. [#8439](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8439) - [GHSA-f9cv-gfvg-3464](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-f9cv-gfvg-3464)
- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, an authenticated user with write access could write files into a repository's `.git` directory through a crafted tree path. [#8408](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8408) - [GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8)
- _Security:_ Argument injection through a crafted commit or branch reference on several repository API endpoints allowed an authenticated user with read access to leak internal server details to the error logs. [#8393](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8393) - [GHSA-mxrh-2rxr-6mqc](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-mxrh-2rxr-6mqc)
- _Security:_ Argument injection through a crafted branch name when creating a pull request allowed an authenticated user with write access to write files to arbitrary paths on the server. [#8390](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8390) - [GHSA-2grc-qr7q-6m36](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-2grc-qr7q-6m36)
- Organization member and team actions, such as removing a member or leaving a team, failed with "Bad Request: no CSRF token present". [#8399](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/8399)

<details>
<summary>Previous patch releases</summary>

## 0.14.3

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Reverse proxy authentication header was honored from any remote address, allowing user impersonation when Gogs was reachable directly. The header is now only trusted from addresses listed in `[auth] TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`. [#8264](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8264) - [GHSA-w6j9-vw59-27wv](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-w6j9-vw59-27wv)
- _Security:_ Server-side request forgery in webhook deliveries via HTTP redirects to local network addresses. [#8263](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8263) - [GHSA-c4v7-xg93-qf8g](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-c4v7-xg93-qf8g)
- _Security:_ Denial of service when rendering issue references against a malformed external issue tracker URL format. [#8312](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8312) - [GHSA-4j89-2c4f-44c6](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-4j89-2c4f-44c6)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through Markdown links with `javascript:` URLs. [#8319](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8319) - [GHSA-jq8v-rmf6-65jw](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-jq8v-rmf6-65jw)
- _Security:_ Missing authorization check on the attachment download endpoint allowed anyone who knew (or guessed) an attachment UUID to download files belonging to private repositories. [#8320](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8320) - [GHSA-p9f5-h3rx-j5qw](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-p9f5-h3rx-j5qw)
- _Security:_ Organization team and member management actions accepted GET requests, allowing a logged-in owner to be tricked into adding an attacker to the Owners team via a crafted link. [#8321](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8321) - [GHSA-pwx3-qcgw-vh7h](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-pwx3-qcgw-vh7h)
- _Security:_ SSRF via mirror address update bypassing clone address validation. [#8225](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8225) - [GHSA-wv27-2vqp-j7g5](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-wv27-2vqp-j7g5)
- _Security:_ Open redirect on login and other post-action flows via the `redirect_to` query parameter. [#8322](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8322) - [GHSA-xxhq-69mf-w8cr](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xxhq-69mf-w8cr)
- _Security:_ Privilege escalation to repository owner via collaboration access mode update. [#8227](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8227) - [GHSA-4565-r4x7-hg8j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-4565-r4x7-hg8j)
- _Security:_ SSRF in repository migration and recurring mirror sync via HTTP redirects and stale host validation on stored mirror URLs. [#8324](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8324) - [GHSA-g2f5-gjr4-qjvm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-g2f5-gjr4-qjvm)
- _Security:_ Remote command execution via pull request rebase merges with crafted branch names. [#8301](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301) - [GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in the milestone dropdown on the new issue page via crafted milestone names. [#8325](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8325) - [GHSA-vcm5-gvmp-78mp](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vcm5-gvmp-78mp)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through `data:text/html` URIs that bypassed the sanitizer. [#8326](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8326) - [GHSA-3w28-36p9-w929](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-3w28-36p9-w929)
- _Security:_ Write-level collaborators could change admin-only repository settings (issue tracker, wiki, mirror sync) via API. [#8327](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8327) - [GHSA-268j-37xf-pp52](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-268j-37xf-pp52)
- _Security:_ Password reset tokens stayed valid for the account-activation lifetime, ignoring `[auth] RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES`. [#8328](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8328) - [GHSA-5c3f-6486-3g7g](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-5c3f-6486-3g7g)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through raw HTML in markdown cells. [#8330](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8330) - [GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp)
- _Security:_ Read-only Git HTTP access could be confused with write access during repository pushes. [#8331](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8331) - [GHSA-wmfg-5p4h-5fw3](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-wmfg-5p4h-5fw3)
- _Security:_ Arbitrary file write outside the repository working tree via crafted upload filename routed through a committed directory symlink. [#8332](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8332) - [GHSA-89mr-xqfv-758m](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-89mr-xqfv-758m)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository disclosure of Git LFS object contents by binding a known OID to another repository without proving possession of the bytes. [#8333](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8333) - [GHSA-6p9m-q3jp-47h4](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-6p9m-q3jp-47h4)
- _Security:_ Remote code execution via path traversal in organization names accepted through the API. [#8334](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8334) - [GHSA-c39w-43gm-34h5](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-c39w-43gm-34h5)
- _Security:_ Stalled SSH handshakes pinned a file descriptor and goroutine indefinitely. The built-in SSH server now drops connections that do not complete the handshake within 15 seconds. [#8335](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8335) - [GHSA-xp79-5mx3-jx52](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xp79-5mx3-jx52)
- _Security:_ Organization metadata and team list endpoints were reachable without authentication. [#8336](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8336) - [GHSA-744x-3838-5r56](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-744x-3838-5r56)

## 0.14.2

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Denial of service in repository and wiki file listing pages via crafted file names. [#8116](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8116) - [GHSA-3qq3-668m-v9mj](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-3qq3-668m-v9mj)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository LFS object overwrite via missing content hash verification. [#8166](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8166) - [GHSA-gmf8-978x-2fg2](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-gmf8-978x-2fg2)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS via data URI in issue comments. [#8174](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8174) - [GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j)
- _Security:_ Release tag option injection in release deletion. [#8175](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8175) - [GHSA-v9vm-r24h-6rqm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-v9vm-r24h-6rqm)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in branch and wiki views through author and committer names. [#8176](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8176) - [GHSA-vgvf-m4fw-938j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vgvf-m4fw-938j)
- _Security:_ DOM-based XSS via issue meta selection on the issue page. [#8178](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8178) - [GHSA-vgjm-2cpf-4g7c](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vgjm-2cpf-4g7c)
- Unable to update files via web editor and API. [#8184](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8184)

### Removed

- Support for passing API access tokens via URL query parameters (`token`, `access_token`). Use the `Authorization` header instead. [#8177](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8177) - [GHSA-x9p5-w45c-7ffc](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-x9p5-w45c-7ffc)

## 0.14.1

### Added

- Support comparing tags in addition to branches. [#6141](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/6141)
- Show file name in browser tab title when viewing files. [#5896](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/5896)
- Support using TLS for Redis session provider using `[session] PROVIDER_CONFIG = ...,tls=true`. [#7860](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/7860)
- Support expanading values in `app.ini` from environment variables, e.g. `[database] PASSWORD = ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}`. [#8057](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8057)
- Support custom logout URL that users get redirected to after sign out using `[auth] CUSTOM_LOGOUT_URL`. [#8089](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8089)
- Start publishing next-generation, security-focused Docker image via `gogs/gogs:next-latest`, which will become the default image distribution (`gogs/gogs:latest`) starting 0.16.0. While not all container options support have been added in the next-generation image, the use of current legacy Docker image is deprecated, it will be published as `gogs/gogs:legacy-latest` starting 0.16.0, and be completely removed no earlier than 0.17.0. [#8061](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8061)

### Changed

- The required Go version to compile source code changed to 1.25.
- The build tag `cert` has been removed, and the `gogs cert` subcommand is now always available. [#7883](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/7883)
- Switched to pure-Go SQLite driver, CGO is no longer required to compile Gogs. [#7882](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7882)
- Updated Mermaid JS to 11.9.0. [#8009](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8009)
- Halt the repository creation and leave the directory untouched if the repository root already exists. [#8091](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8091)

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Unauthenticated file upload. [#8128](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8128) - [GHSA-fc3h-92p8-h36f](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-fc3h-92p8-h36f)
- _Security:_ Protected branch bypass in web UI. [#8124](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8124) - [GHSA-2c6v-8r3v-gh6p](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-2c6v-8r3v-gh6p)
- _Security:_ Authorization bypass allows cross-repository label modification. [#8123](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8123) - [GHSA-cv22-72px-f4gh](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-cv22-72px-f4gh)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository comment deletion. [#8119](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8119) - [GHSA-jj5m-h57j-5gv7](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-jj5m-h57j-5gv7)
- 500 error on repository watchers and stargazers pages when using MSSQL. [#5482](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/5482)
- Submodules using `ssh://` protocol and a port number are not rendered correctly. [#4941](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/4941)
- Missing link to user profile on the first commit in commits history page. [#7404](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7404)
- Unable to delete or display files with special characters in their names. [#7596](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7596)
- Docker healthcheck fails when `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables are set. [#7529](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7529)

</details>

data.name: v2.2.2
data.body:
### November 12, 2026

SECURITY:

* core/acl: Harden explicit deny rule evaluation by matching requested paths case-insensitively.

CHANGES:

* auth/alicloud: Update plugin to [v0.24.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-alicloud/releases/tag/v0.24.1)
* auth/cf: Update plugin to [v0.24.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-cf/releases/tag/v0.24.1)
* auth/jwt: Update plugin to [v0.27.2](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-jwt/releases/tag/v0.27.2)
* auth/kerberos: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kerberos/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* auth/oci: Update plugin to [v0.22.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-oci/releases/tag/v0.22.1)
* core: Bump Go version to 1.27.4
* core/acl: Fix an issue where explicit deny policy rules were not enforced against case variants of the denied path. Explicit deny rules now also match the requested path case-insensitively, subject to the usual rule specificity. For example, a deny on `secret/data/example` now also denies requests to `secret/data/EXAMPLE`.
* database/couchbase: Update plugin to [v0.17.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-couchbase/releases/tag/v0.17.1)
* database/elasticsearch: Update plugin to [v0.21.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-elasticsearch/releases/tag/v0.21.1)
* database/mongodbatlas: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-mongodbatlas/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* database/redis: Update plugin to [v0.9.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-redis/releases/tag/v0.9.1)
* database/snowflake: Update plugin to [v0.17.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-snowflake/releases/tag/v0.17.1)
* proxy/agent: Custom plugins or integrations that return interactive HTML through Agent or Proxy will no longer render interactively in a browser.
* secrets/alicloud: Update plugin to [v0.23.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-alicloud/releases/tag/v0.23.1)
* secrets/azure: Update plugin to [v0.28.5+ent](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-azure/releases/tag/v0.28.5+ent)
* secrets/keymgmt: Update plugin to [v0.20.2+ent](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-keymgmt/releases/tag/v0.20.2+ent)
* secrets/mongodbatlas: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-mongodbatlas/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* secrets/terraform: Update plugin to [v0.15.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-terraform/releases/tag/v0.15.1)

IMPROVEMENTS:

* core: Include the namespace ID in mount setup failure logs
* core: Update github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 to v4.1.6 and golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0
* ui: Show "Never" as the last Vault rotation on the LDAP role credentials page when a static role has not been rotated, instead of a date in year 0001.

BUG FIXES:

* Transit (enterprise): Fix cache bug that led to non-zero `auto_rotate_period` values being written to the cache with managed keys
* agent/pki-external-ca (enterprise): Fix premature certificate reissuance on auto-auth re-authentication so certificate renewal respects `percent_renew_before_expiry` instead of being triggered by token updates.
* audit: Fixed a bug where Vault returned HTTP 500 when a large response (e.g. a PKI ?help=1 request) could not be written to a syslog audit device due to the OS Unix datagram socket size limit (EMSGSIZE / ENOBUFS). The syslog sink now splits oversized audit payloads into safe-sized chunks and retries transiently full socket buffers.
* audit: Fixes a panic that can occur when audit broker not initialized during teardown.
* auth/approle: Reject expired SecretIDs during login instead of relying on periodic tidy cleanup.
* auth/spiffe (enterprise): Fix an issue where renewable tokens were not being renewed
* core (enterprise): Fix a panic and partial namespace creation when the root agent-registry mount is unavailable
* core/census (enterprise): Fix the `previous_month_complete` census gauge reporting 0 in the first month after the billing start date auto-rolls, so the previous billing cycle's final client count is reported.
* core/plugin: Fix an issue where external secrets engine and auth plugins remained read-only after failing to load during startup or unseal. Operators can now restore the missing binary or registration and reload the plugin to resume writes without restarting Vault.
* core: Fix an issue where policy path matching could be inconsistent for requests that differ only by a trailing slash.
* identity: Use the reporting conflict resolver only while reloading in case-sensitive mode, to avoid collecting duplicates after unseal.
* pki-external-ca: Fix premature deletion of revoked certificate records during tidy; revoked orders are now retained until the certificate's NotAfter date rather than the ACME order expiry
* secrets/azure: Continue permanent application cleanup when the active application is already absent, allowing later cleanup attempts to retry the purge.
* secrets/azure: Retry transient Microsoft Graph 403/404 errors when adding newly created service principals to Azure groups.
* secrets/kv: Fixed an issue in KV v1 where writing a secret path containing consecutive slashes caused list operations to return "/" as a directory entry, producing an infinite loop in the Vault UI breadcrumb.
* tpm: tpm auth now respects the InsecureSkipVerify option
* ui: Fix the database overview page to list both dynamic and static roles and allow credential generation, and restore the Roles tab for users with only static-role permissions
* ui: fixes pagination on entities list table
* vault proxy: Support tpm method in the auto_auth block to match parity with agent.

data.name: Release v2.15.3
data.body:
## Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

### Go Version

- 1.27.4

### Dependencies

- github.com/nats-io/jwt/v2 v2.8.3 (#8861)
- github.com/nats-io/nkeys v0.4.17 (#8861)
- github.com/antithesishq/antithesis-sdk-go v0.9.0-default-no-op (#8885)
- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.4 (#8885)
- golang.org/x/sys v0.50.0 (#8885)

### Added

General

- Account subject mappings, imports, exports and leafnode remote permissions now support the `{{account-hash()}}`, `{{account-hash-import()}}` and `{{account-hash-leaf-remote()}}` subject mapping functions (#8670)
- TLS configuration now supports `verify: optional`, and the command line supports `--tlsverify=optional`, verifying client certificates when provided while allowing clients without certificates (#8812, contributed by @macphersonjamie)
- Leafnode connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` (#8718, contributed by @stackedbyaradhya)
- Gateway connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` (#8717, contributed by @stackedbyaradhya)
- The command line now supports `-t --test_reload <file>` to check whether a configuration change can be reloaded or requires a restart, returning exit code 3 when a restart is required; embedded servers can use `CheckReload` and `CheckReloadOptions` (#8829)

Monitoring

- Healthz now supports `leaf-remotes-connected=true`, returning an unavailable status until every enabled solicited leafnode remote is connected (#8735, contributed by @edjeffreys)

### Improved

General

- Route, gateway and leafnode connection logs now include remote destinations (#8755)
- Account import failures now log their reasons at error level (#8771)
- Gateway connections now validate protocol operations consistently with route connections (#8780)

JetStream

- Filestore subject matching and pending message calculations now avoid unnecessary scans and stop earlier when matches are found (#8784, #8803, #8806, #8808, #8813)
- Looking up the last sequence for a subject no longer requires loading the message, reducing work for stream operations and fast batch publishing (#8807)
- Filestore scans with single or multiple subject filters now avoid copying messages that do not match (#8854, #8855)
- Consumer redelivery queues no longer copy all remaining entries on each dequeue, reducing delays to delivery and acknowledgement processing with large redelivery backlogs (#8635, contributed by @as-clearview)
- Filestore scans with multiple subject filters now handle message blocks with many deleted messages more efficiently (#8864)
- Filestore subject scans and filtered pending-message counts now skip contiguous ranges of deleted messages (#8875, #8877)
- Loading filestore message blocks now avoids fully parsing messages when checking for `Nats-TTL` and `Nats-Schedule` headers (#8870, contributed by @adios-404)

### Fixed

General

- Lame duck mode is no longer skipped when `SIGTERM` follows `SIGUSR2` immediately, and servers continue to deliver their own replies after the lame duck event (#8750)
- Configuration reloads no longer disconnect clients authorized by auth callout when their permissions have not changed (#8759)
- Auth callout user JWT names and tags are now propagated to client information (#8720, contributed by @steve-weiland)
- Configuration reloads now wait for server startup to finish (#8728, contributed by @edelmanjm)
- Connz totals now correctly reflect user, MQTT client and subject filters (#8753, contributed by @NitinKumar004)
- Connz and Subsz pagination no longer repeats or skips entries, including connections with equal sort values (#8770)
- Windows PDH queries are now released if performance counter initialization fails (#8777, contributed by @cvas22)
- Auth callout requests are now rejected safely when system account eventing has already shut down (#8804, contributed by @davidfarah2003)
- Wildcard characters inside a subject token are no longer treated as wildcard tokens or allowed to cause subject matching collisions (#8765)
- Account updates no longer unnecessarily recheck importers when export revocations have not changed (#8851)
- Configuration checks with `-t` now apply command line flags and validate options consistently with server startup (#8829)
- Duplicate non-queue subscriptions received over routes no longer leak interest to leafnodes and gateways (#8846)
- Gateway accounts in interest-only mode no longer stop receiving messages when an in-flight message races with removal of the last subscription (#8853, contributed by @paulwe)
- Encrypted auth callouts are now rejected when the server has no XKey available (#8878)

JetStream

- Consumer info requests no longer report success for assignments that have not been committed (#8741)
- Push consumers with a `RateLimit` no longer stall indefinitely when a message exceeds the rate limiter burst size (#8748)
- Stream scale-up from R1 can now make progress under continuous writes, and scale-down no longer stalls on peers that were never added as members (#8762)
- Stalled stream restores now report failure through the restore completion advisory, consistently with other failed restores (#8691, contributed by @akarazhev)
- JetStream no longer shuts down prematurely during server shutdown or lame duck mode (#8708, contributed by @yousefissa)
- Raft meta-group setup failures now stop the write-ahead log instead of leaking it (#8722, contributed by @clwluvw)
- Leader transfers now retry promptly when the selected successor is slow, prefer caught-up peers and avoid persisting the same term and vote twice (#8751)
- Interest retention cleanup no longer purges a stream when a consumer has a zero check floor, and compaction is bounded by the stream's last sequence (#8757, contributed by @tsite)
- Filestore `MultiLastSeqs` no longer skips matching subjects (#8769)
- Fixed a directory creation race when enabling account storage concurrently with stream creation (#8767, contributed by @ansh0014)
- Deleting a stream no longer races with account directory cleanup (#8774, contributed by @ansh0014)
- Sources no longer discard the remainder of a batch when one sourced message is rejected (#8772)
- Pull requests made through service imports are now removed when the requester loses interest, even while response wildcard interest remains (#8797)
- Consumers no longer deliver while a reset is in flight or report later deliveries in reset responses, and durable mirrors and sources no longer skip messages after a reset or stale delivery (#8802)
- Memory store purge and last-sequence scans are now bounded by the possible sequence range (#8815)
- Raft health checks now wait for the leader's initial data to be applied, remain stable between heartbeats and during leader changes, and allow newly assigned replicated streams and consumers time to start (#8817)
- Resuming a paused consumer now wakes its delivery loop immediately, allowing pending pull requests and push deliveries to proceed (#8791)
- `AckAll` acknowledgements are no longer ignored after acknowledging a redelivered message (#8839)
- Filestore recovery failures now return the original error instead of panicking, preserve existing stream data and avoid incorrect storage accounting (#8844, contributed by @rleungx)
- Streams and consumers with unsupported configuration values are now correctly marked offline, updates are rejected by meta leaders that cannot support them, and internal proposals preserve their stored configurations (#8843)
- Paused Raft followers can now request newer snapshots and compact their logs while catching up, preventing unbounded log growth and excessive memory use when replay resumes (#8842)
- Filestore recovery scans now persist per-message state indexes even if no new messages are published, and backward subject scans skip irrelevant blocks (#8849)
- Clustered health checks now report write errors on R1 streams (#8850)
- Removed peers in unmanaged Raft groups can no longer rejoin as leader (#8847)
- Scaling streams and consumers to or from R1 no longer loses writes or acknowledgements during the transition or violates atomic batch guarantees (#8766)
- Resetting consumers with the `last_per_subject` delivery policy now rebuilds the last-message-per-subject selection, preserves the correct delivery position after leader changes, and reports lookup errors instead of ignoring them (#8862)
- Filestore encryption key creation failures no longer leak file descriptors (#8873)
- The filestore access-time worker now shuts down reliably when the last store closes, preventing worker leaks or stopped timestamp updates when stores are reopened (#8794, contributed by @ajaykr0905)
- Rebuilding message deduplication state now skips deleted messages and expires restored entries at the end of their original duplicate window (#8874)
- Restoring a stream from a V2 snapshot now rebuilds message deduplication state, restoring duplicate detection and `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` checks without a server restart (#8871, contributed by @muhadyan)

Leafnodes

- Isolated spoke leafnodes no longer forward downstream leafnode interest to their hubs, and avoid collecting interest that cannot be forwarded (#8749)
- Leafnode interest is now withdrawn correctly when an outbound gateway connection closes (#8758)
- Fixed a data race when reading route leafnode origin support (#8779)
- Leafnode `deny_imports` no longer drops replies to hub requests, and account JWT or default permission updates no longer lose leafnode interest or reset permissions incorrectly (#8800)
- Leafnode connections no longer become stale when a hub sends many subscriptions during connection setup (#8811)
- Leafnode connections closed during acceptance are now removed from the server's connection list, preventing inflated leafnode counts and stale Leafz entries (#8838, contributed by @rnikhori)
- Enforcing account leafnode connection limits no longer risks a deadlock when processing remote connection counts (#8873)

Routes

- Routes without pooling now validate the route pool index correctly (#8782)

### Complete Changes

data.name: v6.2.0
data.body:
### Security
- Addresses CVE-2026-121885, untrusted image labels could be used to trick podman auto-update into restarting incorrect systemd units [GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/security/advisories/GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr).
- Addresses CVE-2026-111361, malicious containers images could be able to bypass Digest and Signature validation [GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/security/advisories/GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw).
- Addresses CVE-2026-123876, default seccomp profile socket deny rule could be bypass by a malicious container.

### Features
- The `podman push` command now supports a new option, `--platform`, which selects and pushes a single platform-specific manifest instead of the entire list.
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--validate`, which determines how unrecognized YAML fields are handled ([#18332](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/18332)).
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--label`, to set labels on created containers, pods, volumes, and secrets ([#26450](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26450)).
- The `podman kube play` command can now create multiple pods if more than 1 replica is requested by a deployment using the new `--multiple-pods` option ([#26769](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26769)).
- The `podman kube play --build` command now supports building images from subdirectories of the main context directory ([#28148](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28418)).
- Quadlet `.container` files now support a new key, `Umask`, to set the default umask for the created container ([#25278](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25278)).
- All Quadlet files now support a new key, `SetMountsDependency`, configuring whether the generated unit will use `RequiresMountsFor`, `WantsMountsFor`, or no dependency at all on required source paths ([#29946](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29946)).
- The `podman farm list` command now supports two new options, `--quiet`, which will print only the names of active farms, and `--noheading`, which omits column headers from the output.
- The `podman artifact ls` command now supports two new options, `--format=json`, which will output machine-readable JSON, and `--quiet`, which prints only artifact digests.
- The `podman create` command now supports a new option, `--passwd`, to add entries to `/etc/passwd` in the container (this has previously been available with `podman run`).
- The `podman info` command now includes detailed information on the features supported by OCI runtimes.
- The `podman events --filter` command now supports a new filter, `network=`, to filter to events pertaining to a specific network ([#29387](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29387)).
- The `podman auto-update` command has been enabled on the remote Podman client.
- The `StartInterval` field in image healthcheck configuration is now respected, allowing images to configure startup healthchecks ([#27724](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27724)).
- The `podman image scp` command now supports two new options, `--compression-format` and `--compression-level`, to compress data during transfer ([#23192](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/23192)).
- The `podman auto-update` command now supports a new option, `--filter`, to selectively update only containers that match the given filters.
- The `podman ps --sort` command now allows sorting by pod.
- The `podman ps --filter` command now supports a new filter, `status!`, which matches containers not in the given state ([#21398](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/21398)).

### Changes
- Podman now requires Go v1.26 or higher to build.
- The Podman machine WSL provider now has native systemd support, existing machines continue to be supported for now with our old custom systemd setup. We require at least WSL version 2.5.1 now, although we recommend using at least 2.7.5 for proper nftables networking support.
- The `podman kube play` command now uses the `securityContext.seccompProfile` fields in Kubernetes YAML for Seccomp configuration. Support for the existing annotation-based configuration of Seccomp is now deprecated, and will be removed with Podman 7.0.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now includes three new fields, `DNSNames` (containing all names the container can be accessed via), `IsInitCtr` (whether the container is an init container), and `InitContainerType` (what type of init container this is, if it is one) ([#29811](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29811)).
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now only includes user-added DNS aliases in the `Aliases` field, which previously displayed all DNS aliases, improving Docker compatibility.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now properly populates the `ConsoleSize` field for running containers ([#28368](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28368)).
- Systemd units created by Podman healthchecks are now named much more clearly (`libpod-healthcheck-$CONTAINERID-$randsuffix.service`) ([#29373](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29373)).
- Signal proxying is now enabled for attached `podman exec` commands. As such, killing a `podman exec` command with Control-C or similar should now also kill the processes started in the container (similar to how `podman run` already works) ([#19486](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/19486)).
- The deprecated `--cpu-rt-period` and `--cpu-rt-runtime` options for `podman create`, `podman run`, `podman update`, and `podman container clone` are now hidden and undocumented. They have not been functional since the removal of cgroups v1 support and will be removed entirely in Podman v7.
- The `--health-startup-interval` option to `podman create`, `podman run`, and `podman update` has a new alias, `--health-start-interval`.
- When a startup healthcheck interval is specified, but no startup healthcheck command, the standard healthcheck command will be used instead.
- When using the `journald` event driver, timestamps are no longer included in logged events, as `journald` includes a timestamp already ([#29835](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29835)).
- Quadlet can now create template instances from instance-specific drop-in directories without requiring an explicit instance file or symlink ([#27636](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27636)).

### Bugfixes
- Fixed a bug where passing an empty file to the `--ignorefile` option to `podman build` would cause the `.dockerignore` or `.containerignore` file in the context directory to be used, instead of not using an ignorefile at all ([#25147](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25147)).
- Fixed a bug where the `Pod=` key in Quadlet `.container` files did not expand the `%N` specifier ([#29108](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29108)).
- Fixed a bug where containers created with `--userns=auto` would report having a `private` user namespace in `podman inspect` after they started, but not when they were first created.
- Fixed a bug where logging was configured too late in the Podman init process to print errors from parsing configuration files ([#25362](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25362)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman system prune --build` command could fail if a build container was removed while it was running.
- Fixed a bug where `copy` events from `podman machine cp` were not properly displayed by the remote Podman client.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman farm build --tag` command would fail if given a tag including a colon ([#25039](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25039)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine init --image` command would fail when given a read-only disk image.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` and `podman machine init --now` commands could hang on Windows systems using the Hyper-V provider if the VM failed to start ([#29455](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29455)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command on Windows (both Hyper-V and WSL providers) would sometimes fail due to leftover processes from previous machines ([#29474](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29474)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command could hang indefinitely if the VM failed to start properly ([#29880](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29880)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command could create a VM that cannot be connected to on Windows if the host was shut down or restarted when the VM was running ([#29971](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29971)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine init` command on Windows when using the Hyper-V provider did not correctly detach the file server process, causing VMs to lose access to host shares when the console that ran `podman machine init` closed ([#29573](http://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29573)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman kube play` command incorrectly handled `emptyDir` volumes with `medium: Memory`, causing them to not be shared between containers in the pod and to ignore the `sizeLimit` parameter ([#29555](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29555)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman kube play` command incorrectly handled authentication credentials in API requests.
- Fixed a bug where volumes created by the `podman volume import` command would not adjust their permissions on being mounted into a container ([#25442](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25442)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman build` command could leak temporary directories if a build failed ([#22642](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/22642)).
- Fixed a bug where containers created with `--userns=keep-id` would use an image-specified user instead of forcing the same UID/GID in use on the host ([#29600](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29600)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client could not function when connecting over SSH to a server which does not support the direct-streamlocal channel type ([#27814](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27814)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman push`, `podman artifact push`, and `podman manifest push` commands would push an unsigned image instead of failing when the `--sign-by` or `--sign-by-sigstore-private-key` options were used.
- Fixed a bug where creating a container with `--userns=auto` that had overlay volume mounts would fail ([#28758](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28758)).
- Fixed a bug where volume subpaths including a `=` character in the path were handled incorrectly.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client was unable to add subjects to artifacts with the `podman manifest annotate --subject` and `podman manifest add --artifact subject` commands.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman manifest add --artifact` command could hang under some circumstances.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman manifest annotate --os-features` command did not properly save the OS features in the manifest.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman image prune --filter` did not correctly handle filters with values including the `=` character.
- Fixed a bug where Quadlet `.volume` units did not recreate the volume if it was removed in Podman ([#27862](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27862)).
- Fixed a bug where containers with a failing startup healthcheck would not immediately transition to unhealthy when the startup period ended.
- Fixed a bug where containers started with `--sdnotify=healthy` and a `HealthStartPeriod` longer than the unit's `TimeoutStartSec` could be automatically killed by systemd if the healthcheck took an extended period to become healthy ([#27290](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27290)).
- Fixed a bug where the `--pids-limit=0` argument to `podman run` and `podman create` was incorrectly setting a process limit, instead of removing the limit, when the `runc` OCI runtime was in use ([#29826](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29826)).
- Fixed a bug where Quadlet did not search the parent directory of symlinked unit files for drop-in configuration files, which broke using Quadlets defined by root as a rootless user if drop-in overrides were in use ([#29821](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29821)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman ps` and `podman pod ps` commands would fail when the `--format` argument was used with a format string including `.Label` ([#29831](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29831)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman cp` command did not respect volume subpaths when copying into a mounted named or image volumes in a container that is not running ([#29840](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29840) and [#29857](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29857)).
- Fixed a bug where volume plugins were initialized when they were not required, which could cause early-boot containers started by Quadlet to error on missing plugins that the container was not actually using ([#28110](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28110)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman export` command, when run by a rootless user on a container created with `--userns=keep-id`, would create an archive with incorrect UIDs and GIDs ([#29856](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29856)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman system service` command would fail to start when run as a systemd unit and autostarted at the same time as other Podman units ([#29964](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29964)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman events` command would return incomplete output when using the `file` events backend and `--until` specified with a time in the past ([#29579](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29579)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman update` command allowed setting a startup healthcheck on a container without a normal healthcheck.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman secret rm` command would fail when given an ambiguous name that could match multiple possible secrets.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine info` command would report the default VM type and config/image directories, not those used by the current machine.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman inspect` command on containers did not include `CheckpointLog` after a failed container checkpoint ([#25154](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25154)).

### API
- The Libpod API now features a new endpoint, `POST /libpod/autoupdate`, which automatically updates containers with the `io.containers.autoupdate` label.
- The Compat API now features a new endpoint, `GET /distribution/{name}/json`, which inspects an image on a registry ([#17726](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/17726)).
- The Compat Create endpoint for Containers now supports a new field, `HostConfig.Mounts.TmpfsOptions.Options`, to set additional options for tmpfs mounts.
- The Compat Create endpoint for Containers now allows a full Seccomp profile to be passed in the `HostConfig.SecurityOpt` field (instead of a path to a file containing a profile), improving Docker compatibility ([#27710](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27710)).
- The Compat Push endpoint for Images now supports a new query parameter, `platform`, to push only a single platform-specific manifest instead of the entire list.
- The Compat Info endpoint now includes the status of active OCI runtimes.
- Fixed a bug where the Libpod Create endpoint for Containers required that the `auto` userns mode also specify full UID/GID mappings for the created container.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Create endpoint for Containers would incorrectly adjust mode when setting tmpfs size.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Create endpoint for Containers would incorrectly treat a healthcheck of `{}` as the user explicitly requesting no healthcheck, instead of using the image's healthcheck as Docker does ([#29467](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29467)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Inspect endpoint for Secrets allowed the `showsecret` query parameter, which should be restricted to Libpod API requests only ([#29570](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29570)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Inspect endpoint for Images included the `Created` field even when it was empty.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat List and Inspect endpoints for Networks did not include `IPRange` in the returned `IPAMConfig` ([#28378](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28378)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat List endpoint for Containers would error when passed a filter including container statuses supported by Docker but not Podman (`dead` and `restarting`) ([#28904](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28904)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Stats endpoint for Containers could panic on containers with a memory reservation, but no memory limit, set ([#29627](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29627)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Stats endpoint for Containers incorrectly populated `system_cpu_usage` and `percpu_stats` when not streaming ([#28761](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28761), [#24730](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/24730), [#25709](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25709), [#29912](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29912)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Info endpoint reported an incorrect cgroup manager when running rootless with the `cgroupfs` cgroup manager ([#27824](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27824)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Attach endpoints for Containers would, when doing a logs-only (`stream=0` and `logs=1`) attach, incorrectly reinitialize the container, changing its exit code and status ([#29664](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29664
)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Update endpoints would incorrectly clear a container's restart policy when it was omitted from the request ([#29790](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29790)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Start endpoints for Exec sessions would return an error when trying to start an exec session with no standard streams attached without specifying `Detach=true`.
- Fixed a bug where the Libpod Generate Kube endpoint returned the wrong content type ([#29674](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29674)).
- Numerous fixes to the API's Swagger documentation have been made to ensure it accurately documents the REST API.

### Misc
- Fixed a number of low-level resource leaks in various parts of Podman.
- Waiting for `gvproxy` to start when starting a `podman machine` VM now uses a notification socket, instead of polling, improving reliability and startup time.
- Updated documentation for the `--image-volume` option to `podman create` and `podman run` to remove the deprecated `bind` option and add the new default, `anonymous`, which was not shown as a valid option. Using the deprecated `bind` option now prints a warning.
- Updated Buildah to v1.46.0
- Updated Common to v0.70.0
- Updated Image to v5.42.1
- Updated Storage to v1.64.2

## 🚀 New features and improvements

data.body:
See the full [kOps 1.37 release notes](https://kops.sigs.k8s.io/releases/1.37-notes/) for details, including breaking changes and deprecations.

## Highlights

* **Kubernetes 1.37 support**, with etcd 3.7.3 as the default for Kubernetes 1.37 clusters
* **Private asset repositories in cloud object storage**: `s3://`, `gs://`, and `azureblob://` URLs for `KOPS_BASE_URL` and `spec.assets.fileRepository`, with nodes authenticating through their instance identity
* **Smaller and more resilient node bootstrap**: the nodeup download drops from about 120 MB to under 10 MB, through a smaller binary and xz compression, and bootstrap retries failed tasks
* **Container runtime**: containerd 2.3.6 and runc 1.5.1 by default, with containerd configuration version 4; containerd versions older than 2.1.0 are no longer supported
* **Karpenter expansion**: Karpenter v1.15.1, kOps-managed interruption handling (SQS queue and EventBridge rules), root volume settings in `EC2NodeClass`, `instanceRequirements` support, and mixed GPU and non-GPU instance groups
* **Narrower AWS IAM permissions** for the instance roles (Route 53, KMS, EC2, SQS), and no inline policies for roles that need no permissions
* **etcd-manager changes**: bundled etcd images mounted as image volumes, and support for custom etcd versions from a user-supplied image on new clusters
* **Networking**: Calico v3.32.3 with the move to `ClusterNetworkPolicy`, network policy support for AWS VPC CNI, kube-router v2.12.0 with an experimental nftables network policy backend, and kindnet v1.0.3
* **Azure**: bootstrap requests authenticated with signed instance metadata, `kops rolling-update cluster` detection of outdated VMs, and two cloud-controller-manager replicas on highly available control planes
* **Akamai (Linode)**: the experimental provider now manages SSH keys, networks, subnets, instances, and block-storage volumes
* **Component updates**: etcd-manager v3.0.20261022 with etcd 3.5.35/3.6.16/3.7.3, Cilium v1.18.16, AWS VPC CNI v1.23.2, CoreDNS v1.15.0, AWS Load Balancer Controller v3.6.2, cert-manager v1.21.3, cluster-autoscaler v1.37.0
* **Removed**: support for Kubernetes 1.31, gossip DNS (and `protokube`), AWS Classic Load Balancers for the API, and Kopeio networking. Migrate with kOps 1.36 before the upgrade

data.name: Istio 1.32.0
data.body: [Release Notes](https://istio.io/latest/news/releases/1.32.x/announcing-1.32/)

* [CHANGE] Promote the `auto-gomemlimit` feature flag to the `--auto-gomemlimit` command-line flag. This is a breaking change: the `--enable-feature=auto-gomemlimit` option has been removed. #5464
* [CHANGE] Remove the deprecated `types` package in favor of the `alert` package. #5585
* [CHANGE] eventrecorder: Every output now requires a `name`. This is a breaking change: configurations with unnamed outputs fail to load. The name identifies the output in metrics and logs instead of its URL, broker or topic. #5393
* [CHANGE] eventrecorder: The output data format now uses the new `events/v2` schema. This is a breaking change: alert labels, alert annotations, group labels, silence annotations, and muted-alert labels are JSON maps, and protobuf consumers must use the new schema. #5409, #5500
* [FEATURE] Add a distroless container image. #5258
* [FEATURE] amtool: Look up the default config file in `%APPDATA%` and `%ProgramData%` on Windows. #5073
* [FEATURE] api: Add an experimental ConnectRPC API served alongside `/api/v2/` under the version-neutral `/api/` prefix, exposing the Connect, gRPC, and gRPC-Web protocols plus the gRPC Health Checking Protocol and server reflection. The first service is `status.v3.StatusService`. #5377, #5506, #5507, #5508, #5509
* [FEATURE] incidentio: Add templated `metadata` field. #5022
* [FEATURE] pagerduty: Report more specific failure reasons in `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total`. #5659
* [FEATURE] rocketchat: Add `message_text` option to set the message text shown in desktop and push notifications. #5595
* [FEATURE] slack: Add `post_updates_to_thread` option to post subsequent notifications of an alert group as replies in the thread of the initial message. #5540
* [FEATURE] telegram: Add `timeout` option to limit how long a notification request may take. #5127
* [FEATURE] telegram: Count only visible HTML text toward the message length limit, excluding link URLs. #5499
* [FEATURE] template: Add `addDuration` function to shift a timestamp by a duration such as `-30m` and return it in Unix milliseconds. #5550
* [FEATURE] template: Allow the `join` function to accept slices and arrays of any type. #5233
* [FEATURE] timeinterval: Allow weekday ranges to wrap around the end of the week, e.g. `friday:monday`. #5579
* [FEATURE] ui: Make the creator and comment of a silence optional, matching the API. #5471
* [FEATURE] ui: Serve the new Mantine UI at `/ui/` alongside the existing UI. #5502, #5538, #5539, #5537
* [ENHANCEMENT] Compute alert fingerprints once at ingestion instead of on every mute check, reducing CPU usage and allocations. #5583
* [ENHANCEMENT] api: Speed up `/api/v2/alerts/groups` by evaluating mutes only once per alert and group. #5674
* [ENHANCEMENT] cluster: Fix the `memeberlist` typo in error messages. #5472
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Add a Gotify example using a custom webhook payload. #5408, #5498
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Add a reusable HTML email template example. #5391
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Clarify the usage of the KV `Remove` template function. #5297
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Clarify which route options are inherited by child routes. #5565
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Correct the PagerDuty default config. #5397
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Document OAuth2 support in the `http_config` of `jira_config`. #5571
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Document VictorOps custom fields. #5399
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Document `project` and `issue_type` in `jira_config` as templated strings. #5549
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Document `victorops_api_key` and `victorops_api_key_file` in the global config. #5168
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Fix `rocketchat_config` defaults and field types. #5591
* [ENHANCEMENT] docs: Fix the `tracing` config key, which was misspelled as `traciing`. #5437
* [ENHANCEMENT] notify: Add the receiver name to the log message for failed notifications. #5401
* [ENHANCEMENT] silences: Reduce allocations when computing the `alertmanager_silences` metric. #5460
* [ENHANCEMENT] victorops: Use Splunk On-Call branding in documentation and error messages without renaming configuration fields. #5402
* [BUGFIX] api: Report alerts muted by time intervals as of the time of the request instead of the last group flush, matching silences and inhibitions. #5661
* [BUGFIX] cluster: Downgrade memberlist to v0.5.4 to fix `Failed to read remote state: user state length (...) exceeds limit` errors. #5640
* [BUGFIX] config: Fix merging of global configs for the smtp, opsgenie, victorops and rocketchat notifiers. #5448, #5457
* [BUGFIX] discord: Retry notifications on HTTP 429 (rate limited) instead of dropping them. #5496
* [BUGFIX] httpserver: Fix the `/-/reload` endpoint getting stuck when the client cancels the request. #5234
* [BUGFIX] notify: Wait the full backoff interval before retrying a notification that failed slowly. #5497, #5389, #5553
* [BUGFIX] opsgenie: Respect the notification timeout and tracing span for the update-message request sent when `update_alerts` is enabled. #5465
* [BUGFIX] pagerduty: Report the failure reason of Events API v1 requests in `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total` instead of `reason="other"`. #5505
* [BUGFIX] pushover: Trim whitespace from `token_file` and `user_key_file` contents so keys stored in files with a trailing newline are accepted. #5590
* [BUGFIX] silences: Treat a silence as expired at exactly its end time, consistent with the API. #5665
* [BUGFIX] silences: Use a single evaluation time for each read or write of silences. #5666
* [BUGFIX] slack: Avoid a panic when `update_message` relies on `global.slack_api_url`. #5589
* [BUGFIX] slack: Retry notifications on HTTP 429 (rate limited) and honor the `Retry-After` header instead of dropping them. #5048
* [BUGFIX] telegram: Redact the bot token from logged notification errors. #5254
* [BUGFIX] telegram: Report the failure reason in `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total`. #5375
* [BUGFIX] template: Preserve quoted numeric strings as strings in templated JSON fields. #5098
* [BUGFIX] timeinterval: Fix negative `days_of_month` resolving one day early in months with a DST transition. #5447
* [BUGFIX] timeinterval: Reject month numbers outside 1-12. #5626
* [BUGFIX] webex: Fix a panic when truncating long notifications containing non-ASCII characters. #5544
* [BUGFIX] webex: Retry notifications on HTTP 429 (rate limited) and honor the `Retry-After` header instead of dropping them. #5548
* [BUGFIX] wechat: Report template errors in `corp_id` and `api_secret` instead of sending a token request with empty values. #5688

data.body:
## Improvements
**[Agent]** Enhanced Reactor tracing — propagate unsampled traces across publishOn, subscribeOn, delay, and interval (#14604)
**[Agent]** Propagate unsampled traces across Reactor subscribe and retry (#14594)
**[Agent]** Propagate unsampled traces across coroutine dispatch (#14592)
**[Agent]** Added user-supplied URI template support for URI stat in the Jetty plugins (#14546)
**[Agent]** Added serviceName to the span event ContextData
**[Collector]** Apply the durability setting to SpanChunk (#14544)
**[Web]** Added a search box to the sidebar service selector
**[Web]** Added a search box to the server map service selector
**[Web]** Switched the alarm modules from thymeleaf to thymeleaf-spring6 (#14534)

## Bug Fixes
**[Agent]** Fixed a class retransform issue by keeping the original constant pool indices when rewriting a class from its class file (#9246)
**[Agent]** Fixed a Base64 decoding compatibility issue by downgrading commons-codec to 1.22.1 (#14605)
**[Agent]** Fixed an unnecessary retransform by skipping Spring beans that declare no method to intercept
**[Agent]** Fixed the trace block depth in DisableTrace and DisableChildTrace traceBlockEnd()
**[Web]** Fixed the DEFAULT servicemap not applying the search option (#14600)
**[Web]** Fixed the server map right-click handlers to read the latest disableMenu state
**[Web]** Fixed the Apdex hover popup to attach to the side of the node that has room
**[Web]** Fixed the Apdex and service group popups disappearing when the server map menu is disabled
**[Web]** Fixed an extra drawer scroll when viewing servers
**[Web]** Fixed the group-by remove button showing when the error table cannot remove a group
**[Web]** Fixed focus to return to the service search box with ArrowUp from the first result

## Security
**[none]** Bumped fastjson from 1.2.83 to 1.2.84 to fix CVE-2026-16723 (RCE under the default configuration) (#14584)
**[Web]** Bumped handlebars, storybook, and shell-quote to fix critical vulnerabilities
**[Web]** Bumped vite, zod, and transitive dependencies to fix high vulnerabilities
**[Web]** Bumped postcss-selector-parser to 7.1.7 to fix a moderate vulnerability
**[Web]** Reported by @Hamaecco: Reject admin API calls when admin.password is not set (#14533)
