data.name: v2.15.3
data.body:
# Release v2.15.3

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - If you are using Active Directory Federation Service (AD FS), upgrading to Rancher v2.10.1 or later may cause issues with authentication, requiring manual intervention. These issues are due to the AD FS Relying Party Trust not being able to pick up a signature verification certificate from the metadata. For more information, see [\#48655](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/48655). These issues can be corrected by either of two methods:
>
>   - Updating the Relying Party Trust information from federation metadata (Relying Party Trust → Update from Federation Metadata…​).
>
>   - Directly adding the certificate (Relying Party Trust → Properties → Signature tab → Add → Select the certificate).

Rancher v2.15.3 is the latest patch release of Rancher. This is a Community version release that introduces maintenance updates and bug fixes.

For more information on new features in the general minor release, see the [v2.15.0 release notes](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/releases/tag/v2.15.0).

## Security Fixes for Vulnerabilities

This release addresses the following security issues:

### Rancher

- Fixed a security vulnerability in the Rancher meta proxy endpoint where the destination allowlist was evaluated in a location that could not prevent a request from being forwarded. An authenticated user could cause the Rancher server to send requests to internal services that the allowlist is intended to block and receive the responses. The allowlist is now enforced in the request handler, which rejects disallowed destinations before any connection is made. For more information, see [CVE-2026-88809](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-f9gf-wh3x-jx3v).
- Fixed a security vulnerability in Rancher's RBAC validation where the `inheritedNamespacedRules` field of a `GlobalRole` was not checked for privilege escalation. A user with delegated permissions to manage global roles and global role bindings could grant permissions in downstream clusters that exceeded their own. The `GlobalRole` and `GlobalRoleBinding` admission webhooks now validate this field in the same way as the other permission-carrying fields. For more information, refer to [CVE-2026-88810](https://github.com/rancher/webhook/security/advisories/GHSA-f898-2c8h-r7jc).
- Fixed a security vulnerability in the Rancher Manager meta proxy where the caller's own Rancher credentials were not consistently removed from requests forwarded to third-party cloud provider hosts. A signed-in user's session credential could be sent to a cloud provider during ordinary use of provisioning views, and an API client's Rancher token could be sent when it omitted the proxy's credential selection headers. The proxy now strips the caller's credentials on every request path. For more information, refer to [CVE-2026-88811](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-x82x-2qj6-5rm2).
- Fixed a security vulnerability in Rancher where the authorization check that protects the local cluster shell was not applied to every API route that could reach it. Any authenticated user, including one with no permissions on the `local` cluster, could obtain an unprivileged shell pod on the management cluster, breaking the expected isolation of the management plane. The authorization check is now enforced consistently for all request forms. For more information, see [CVE-2026-104623](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-8x6f-2v58-x6p7).

### Fleet

- Fixed a privilege escalation vulnerability in Fleet's agent management controller, where a Fleet cluster object created by an ordinary user could reference administrative credentials for the Rancher management (`local`) cluster. This allowed an authenticated user holding only the default `user` global role, with no permissions on the local cluster, to gain cluster-admin on the Rancher management cluster and thereby on all managed clusters. Fleet now only accepts a kubeconfig secret from another namespace when the secret is labeled for use by the referencing namespace, and only deploys agents onto the management cluster for its own system clusters. For more information, refer to [CVE-2026-94290](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/security/advisories/GHSA-qfmw-gw96-ffcr).
- Fixed a security vulnerability in Fleet where the cluster identity claimed during cluster registration was not bound to the registration token used for the request. A holder of a valid workspace registration token who knew another cluster's client identifier could obtain credentials for that cluster's Fleet management namespace and disrupt its legitimate agent. Fleet now records the registration token a cluster is registered with and rejects registration requests that claim the same cluster identity with a different token. For more information, refer to [CVE-2026-104615](https://github.com/rancher/fleet/security/advisories/GHSA-gx8v-2929-9q95).

For additional details, see the Security Advisories and CVEs page in Rancher's [documentation](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/reference-guides/rancher-security/security-advisories-and-cves) or in Rancher's GitHub [repository](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories).

## Rancher general

### Major bug fixes

- Fixed an issue where Rancher settings configured using environment variables retained stale values and the `source: env` attribute after the environment variable was removed. When an environment variable is removed, Rancher now clears the stored environment source and value on startup. The setting then reverts to its default value. See See [\#58075](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/58075).

## Cluster provisioning

### Major bug fixes

- Fixed an issue where imported clusters could become unavailable after upgrading Rancher if the cluster agent was redeployed before its registration token was migrated, leaving the agent with an empty token. See [\#58028](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/58028).

- Fixed an issue where provisioned clusters with S3 etcd snapshots could remain stuck during deletion. See [\#57506](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/57506).

## Changes Since v2.15.2

See the full list of [changes](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/compare/v2.15.2%E2%80%A6v2.15.3).

## Install/Upgrade Notes

If you’re installing Rancher for the first time, your environment must fulfill the [installation requirements](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/getting-started/installation-and-upgrade/installation-requirements).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - Rancher now requires the cluster it runs on to have the [Kubernetes API Aggregation Layer](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/apiserver-aggregation/) enabled. This is because Rancher extends Kubernetes with additional APIs by registering its own extension API server. Please note that all versions of Kubernetes supported in this Rancher versions K8s distributions (RKE2/K3s) will have the aggregation layer configured and enabled by default.
>
>   - Refer to the [Extension API Server documentation](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/api/extension-apiserver#aggregation-layer-is-required) and [\#50400](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/50400) for more information.
>
> - Rancher Kubernetes Engine (RKE/RKE1) has reached end of life as of **July 31, 2025**. Rancher versions 2.12.0 and later no longer support provisioning or managing downstream RKE1 clusters. We recommend replatforming RKE1 clusters to RKE2 to ensure continued support and security updates. Learn more about the transition [here](https://www.suse.com/support/kb/doc/?id=000021518).
>
>   - Rancher now has a pre-upgrade validation check for RKE1 resources which fails and lists the RKE1 resources if present. Refer to [\#50286](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/50286) for more information.
>
> - It is crucial that you review the available disk space on your nodes and plan accordingly before upgrading to Rancher v2.12.0 and later to avoid potential disk pressure and pod eviction issues.
>
>   - For additional information, refer to the [UI Server Side Pagination - Disk Space documentation](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/how-to-guides/advanced-user-guides/ui-server-side-pagination#disk-space).
>
> - Rancher now has an enablement option called [`AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED`](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/how-to-guides/advanced-user-guides/enable-api-audit-log#viewing-api-audit-logs:~:text=Description-,AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED,-false%20%2D%20Disables%20the) for API Audit Logs for a Rancher installation.
>
>   - In Rancher versions 2.11.x and earlier, only the `AUDIT_LEVEL` could be set and the default log level (`0`) would disable the audit log. In Rancher versions 2.12.x and later, the default log level (`0`) now only contains the log request and response metadata, and can be set when configuring `AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED`. If installing or upgrading via Helm you can enable the API Audit Logs and specify the log level by applying the following setting to your Helm command: `--set auditLog.enabled=true --set auditLog.level=0`. See the [Enabling the API Audit Log to Record System Events](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/how-to-guides/advanced-user-guides/enable-api-audit-log) documentation and [\#48941](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/48941).

## Changes in Image Artifacts

Image artifact digests are renamed in Rancher v2.12.0, v2.11.4 and v2.10.8. Up until this change, separate image digests files for each operating system and architecture have been maintained for compatibility reasons. With this change, only one file for each operating system is to be provided:

- The `rancher-images-digests-linux-amd64.txt` and `rancher-images-digests-linux-arm64.txt` files are to be renamed to `rancher-images-digests-linux.txt`.

- The `rancher-images-digests-windows-ltsc2019.txt` and `rancher-images-digests-windows-ltsc2022.txt` files are to be renamed to `rancher-images-digests-windows.txt`.

## Upgrade Requirements

- **Creating backups:** [Create a backup](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/how-to-guides/new-user-guides/backup-restore-and-disaster-recovery/back-up-rancher) before you upgrade Rancher. To roll back Rancher after an upgrade, you must first back up and restore Rancher to the previous Rancher version. Because Rancher will be restored to the same state as when the backup was created, any changes post-upgrade will not be included after the restore.

- **Helm version requirements:**

  - To manage Rancher 2.12.x and later, you must upgrade your Helm client to version 3.18 or newer.

  - This change is required to reflect the addition of Kubernetes 1.33 support with this release.

  - Currently, the official [Helm Version Support Policy](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/version_skew/) dictates that only Helm 3.18 supports the proper Kubernetes version range for Rancher 2.12.

- **CNI requirements:**

  - For Kubernetes v1.19 and later, disable firewalld as it’s incompatible with various CNI plugins. See [\#28840](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/28840).

  - When upgrading or installing a Linux distribution that uses nf_tables as the backend packet filter, such as SLES 15, RHEL 8, Ubuntu 20.10, Debian 10, or later, upgrade to RKE v1.19.2 or later to get Flannel v0.13.0. Flannel v0.13.0 supports nf_tables. See Flannel [\#1317](https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/issues/1317).

- **Requirements for air-gapped environments:**

  - When using a proxy in front of an air-gapped Rancher instance, you must pass additional parameters to `NO_PROXY`. See the [documentation](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/getting-started/installation-and-upgrade/other-installation-methods/rancher-behind-an-http-proxy/install-rancher) and issue [\#2725](https://github.com/rancher/docs/issues/2725#issuecomment-702454584).

  - When installing Rancher with Docker in an air-gapped environment, you must supply a custom `registries.yaml` file to the `docker run` command, as shown in the [K3s documentation](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/private-registry). If the registry has certificates, then you’ll also need to supply those. See [\#28969](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/28969#issuecomment-694474229).

## Versions

### Images

- rancher/rancher:v2.15.3

### Tools

- CLI - [v2.15.3](https://github.com/rancher/cli/releases/tag/v2.15.3)

### Kubernetes Versions for RKE2/K3s

- v1.36.5 (Default)

- v1.35.9

- v1.34.12

### Rancher Helm Chart Versions

In Rancher v2.6.0 and later, in the **Apps & Marketplace** UI, many Rancher Helm charts are named with a major version that starts with *100*. This avoids simultaneous upstream changes and Rancher changes from causing conflicting version increments. This also complies with semantic versioning (SemVer), which is a requirement for Helm. You can see the upstream version number of a chart in the build metadata, for example: `100.0.0+up2.1.0`. See [\#32294](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/32294).

## Previous Rancher Behavior Changes

### Previous Rancher Behavior Changes - Rancher General

- **Rancher v2.15.0:**

  - Rancher v2.15 removes support for Kubernetes v1.33. See [\#55306](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/55306).

### Previous Rancher Behavior Changes Changes - Rancher App (Global UI)

- **Rancher v2.15.0:**

  - The option to disable the feature flag `ui-sql-cache` / Vai / Server-Side Pagination (SSP) in the Rancher UI has been removed in preparation for Rancher v2.16, where the feature will always be enabled. See [\#16822](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/16822).

  - **Removal**: Support for Ember-based UI plugins for cluster and node drivers (deprecated since Rancher v2.11.0) is removed in Rancher v2.15.0. Migrate your plugins to the [UI Extensions Framework](https://extensions.rancher.io/). For details, see [\#14005](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/14005).

### Previous Rancher Behavior Changes - K3s and RKE2 Provision

- **Rancher v2.15.0:**

  - By default, the `Standard User` and `Create Clusters` [global permissions](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/v2.15/how-to-guides/new-user-guides/authentication-permissions-and-global-configuration/manage-role-based-access-control-rbac/global-permissions) now allow creating and then updating CAPI infrastructure objects in the `fleet-default` namespace. Note that manually created infrastructure provider identity objects, such as `AWSClusterStaticIdentity` or `VSphereClusterIdentity`, that target the `fleet-default` namespace can be used through CAPI infrastructure objects such as `AWSCluster` or `VsphereCluster`. See [\#53777](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/53777).

  - When using native CAPI infrastructure providers with v2prov, Rancher will now generate the bootstrap cloud-config in the [Jinja format](https://docs.cloud-init.io/en/latest/explanation/format/jinja.html). User-data for regular node drivers with v2prov is unaffected. See [\#53777](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/53777).

### Previous Rancher Behavior Changes - Continuous Delivery (Fleet)

- **Rancher v2.15.0:**

  - **Deprecation**: Fleet will be removing support for `GitRepoRestriction` in a future release, making the use of the Policy resource for configuring multi-tenant environments the only option. See [\#55652](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/55652).

  - **Deprecation**: Fleet support for unauthenticated webhook calls will be removed in a future release, making the setup of a [webhook secret](https://fleet.rancher.io/next/how-tos-for-users/webhook#_3_optional_configure_a_webhook_secret) the only option. See [\#55633](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/55633). == Long-standing Known Issues

### Long-standing Known Issues - Cluster Provisioning

- **Rancher v2.15.1:**

  - Creating or editing v2prov clusters with native CAPI infrastructure providers from the UI can under some failure conditions leave unused infrastructure resources in the management cluster that must be cleaned up manually. See [\#55705](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/55705).

- **Rancher v2.15.0:**

  - Imported clusters cannot reconnect to Rancher if their registration token is rotated while they are disconnected and the grace period ends before they reconnect. The cluster agent logs `400 Bad Request` with the response body `cluster not found`. As a workaround, re-run the registration command from the cluster **Registration** tab on the downstream cluster. To prevent the issue, increase the `crt-default-grace-period-minutes` setting to cover the expected downtime, or disable the `crt-token-ttl-rotation` feature flag. See [\#57078](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/57078).

- Not all cluster tools can be installed on a hardened cluster.

- **Rancher v2.8.1:**

  - When you attempt to register a new etcd/controlplane node in a CAPR-managed cluster after a failed etcd snapshot restoration, the node can become stuck in a perpetual paused state, displaying the error message `[ERROR] 000 received while downloading Rancher connection information. Sleeping for 5 seconds and trying again`. As a workaround, you can unpause the cluster by running `kubectl edit clusters.cluster clustername -n fleet-default` and set `spec.unpaused` to `false`. See [\#43735](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/43735).

### Long-standing Known Issues - RKE2 Provisioning

- **Rancher v2.7.7:**

  - Due to the backoff logic in various components, downstream provisioned K3s and RKE2 clusters may take longer to re-achieve **Active** status after a migration. If you see that a downstream cluster is still updating or in an error state immediately after a migration, please let it attempt to resolve itself. This might take up to an hour to complete. See [\#42834](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/42834).

- **Rancher v2.7.6:**

  - Provisioning RKE2/K3s clusters with added (not built-in) custom node drivers causes provisioning to fail. As a workaround, [fix](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/37074#issuecomment-1664722305) the added node drivers after activating. See [\#37074](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/37074).

### Long-standing Known Issues - K3s Provisioning

- **Rancher v2.7.6:**

  - Provisioning RKE2/K3s clusters with added (not built-in) custom node drivers causes provisioning to fail. As a workaround, [fix](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/37074#issuecomment-1664722305) the added node drivers after activating. See [\#37074](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/37074).

- **Rancher v2.7.2:**

  - Clusters remain in an `Updating` state even when they contain nodes in an `Error` state. See [\#39164](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/39164).

### Long-standing Known Issues - Rancher App (Global UI)

- **Rancher v2.10.0:**

  - After deleting a Namespace or Project in the Rancher UI, the Namespace or Project remains visible. As a workaround, refresh the page. See [\#12220](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/12220).

- **Rancher v2.9.2:**

  - Although system mode node pools must have at least one node, the Rancher UI allows a minimum node count of zero. Inputting a zero minimum node count through the UI can cause cluster creation to fail due to an invalid parameter error. To prevent this error from occurring, enter a minimum node count at least equal to the node count. See [\#11922](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/11922).

- **Rancher v2.7.7:**

  - When creating a cluster in the Rancher UI it does not allow the use of an underscore `_` in the `Cluster Name` field. See [\#9416](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/9416).

- **Rancher v2.6.4:**

  - Deployment securityContext section is missing when a new workload is created. This prevents pods from starting when Pod Security Policy Support is enabled. See [\#4815](https://github.com/rancher/dashboard/issues/4815).

### Long-standing Known Issues - EKS

- **Rancher v2.7.0:**

  - EKS clusters on Kubernetes v1.21 or below on Rancher v2.7 cannot be upgraded. See [\#39392](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/39392).

### Long-standing Known Issues - Authentication

- **Rancher v2.9.0:**

  - There are some known issues with the OpenID Connect provider support:

    - When the generic OIDC auth provider is enabled, and you attempt to add auth provider users to a cluster or project, users are not populated in the dropdown search bar. This is expected behavior as the OIDC auth provider alone is not searchable. See [\#46104](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/46104).

    - When the generic OIDC auth provider is enabled, auth provider users that are added to a cluster/project by their username are not able to access resources upon logging in. A user will only have access to resources upon login if the user is added by their userID. See [\#46105](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/46105).

    - When the generic OIDC auth provider is enabled and an auth provider user in a nested group is logged into Rancher, the user will see the following error when they attempt to create a Project: `projectroletemplatebindings.management.cattle.io is forbidden: User "u-gcxatwsnku" cannot create resource "projectroletemplatebindings" in API group "management.cattle.io" in the namespace "p-9t5pg"`. However, the project is still created. See [\#46106](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/46106).

### Long-standing Known Issues - Rancher Webhook

- **Rancher v2.7.2:**

  - A webhook is installed in all downstream clusters. There are several issues that users may encounter with this functionality:

    - If you rollback from a version of Rancher v2.7.2 or later, to a Rancher version earlier than v2.7.2, the webhooks will remain in downstream clusters. Since the webhook is designed to be 1:1 compatible with specific versions of Rancher, this can cause unexpected behaviors to occur downstream. The Rancher team has developed a [script](https://github.com/rancher/webhook/wiki/Remove-Webhook-from-downstream-clusters) which should be used after rollback is complete (meaning after a Rancher version earlier than v2.7.2 is running). This removes the webhook from affected downstream clusters. See [\#40816](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/40816).

### Long-standing Known Issues - Virtualization Management (Harvester)

- **Rancher v2.13.1:**

  - When upgrading to Rancher v2.13.1 or higher while using Harvester v1.6.1, users may encounter an issue with their Load Balancers in downstream clusters using the Harvester Cloud Provider, and must perform the following [workaround](https://docs.harvesterhci.io/latest/troubleshooting/rancher#guest-cluster-loadbalancer-ip-is-not-reachable) to instruct Calico to not use any of the IP/interface managed by `kube-vip`. See [\#9767](https://github.com/harvester/harvester/issues/9767).

- **Rancher v2.7.2:**

  - If you’re using Rancher v2.7.2 with Harvester v1.1.1 clusters, you won’t be able to select the Harvester cloud provider when deploying or updating guest clusters. The [Harvester release notes](https://github.com/harvester/release-notes/blob/main/v1.1.2.md#important-information-about-rancher-support) contain instructions on how to resolve this. See [\#3750](https://github.com/harvester/harvester/issues/3750).

### Long-standing Known Issues - Backup/Restore

- When migrating to a cluster with the Rancher Backup feature, the server-url cannot be changed to a different location. It must continue to use the same URL.

- **Rancher v2.13.0:**

  - When performing a rollback from Rancher v2.13.0 to v2.12.3 using the backup and restore operator (BRO), the restore does not complete successfully. See [\#844](https://github.com/rancher/backup-restore-operator/issues/844). To work around this issue, you must scale down your Rancher deployment and uninstall the Webhook chart before performing the restore. For details, refer to this [Knowledge Base article](https://support.scc.suse.com/s/kb/Rolling-back-from-Rancher-v2-13-0-to-v2-12-3?language=en_US).

- **Rancher v2.7.7:**

  - Due to the backoff logic in various components, downstream provisioned K3s and RKE2 clusters may take longer to re-achieve **Active** status after a migration. If you see that a downstream cluster is still updating or in an error state immediately after a migration, please let it attempt to resolve itself. This might take up to an hour to complete. See [\#42834](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/42834).

data.name: 3.3.0(Oct 29th, 2026)
data.body:
# Nacos 3.3.0

Nacos 3.3.0 is a feature iteration release for the Nacos 3.x series. It brings protocol-neutral Agent management and discovery, shared AI resource search, and unified MCP lifecycle management to the stable release.

This release focuses on:

- AI Registry capabilities across Agent, AgentSpec, Skill, Prompt, and MCP resources.
- DNS service discovery and distributed locks.
- Dynamic plugin management and authentication enabled by default.
- Spring Boot 4 and Jackson 3 compatibility, with improved client and server reliability.

The main feature updates include:

- Agent registration, version management, runtime endpoints, RAD discovery, transport negotiation, and Watch/Push through Java SDKs and Console workflows.
- Shared AI resource search with hybrid keyword and vector retrieval, artifact access, and optional relevance filtering.
- MCP draft, review, publish, online/offline, and visibility management, with migration support for historical resources.
- Optional DNS discovery with A, AAAA, and SRV records over UDP and TCP.
- Distributed reentrant and non-reentrant locks with watchdog renewal and Raft consistency.

The stable release also improves Skill metadata consistency across version transitions, extends visibility plugin capabilities, and strengthens Config SDK usability, Console compatibility, and recovery after Naming reconnects and cluster restarts.

These notes are cumulative and include the changes delivered in 3.3.0-BETA and 3.3.0-RC.

---

Detailed changes in this release:

## Feature

- [#50](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/50) Add optional DNS service discovery over UDP and TCP, with A, AAAA, and SRV records, metrics, and configurable external DNS forwarding.
- [#14466](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14466) Add a neutral JSON adapter with Jackson 2 and Jackson 3 runtime support.
- [#14804](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14804) Add protocol-neutral Agent lifecycle management, Console workflows, RAD discovery, runtime endpoints, transport negotiation, Watch/Push, and Java SDKs.
- [#15279](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15279) Add distributed reentrant and non-reentrant locks with watchdog renewal, FIFO waiting, gRPC notifications, Raft consistency, and a Java Lock SDK.
- [#15471](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15471) Support SkillSpector as an AI publish pipeline.
- [#15475](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15475) Add unified dynamic plugin configuration, lifecycle management, runtime updates, deterministic discovery, and Console configuration workflows.
- [#15476](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15476)[#15604](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15604) Add plugin-owned visibility grant and revoke APIs and Console management for Skill and AgentSpec resources.
- [#15541](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15541) Add Agentic Resource Discovery with search, exploration, artifact retrieval, visibility filtering, persistent indexes, and hybrid keyword and vector retrieval.
- [#15640](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15640) Add Linux RISC-V64 compatibility for RocksDB JNI loading and startup.
- [#15761](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15761) Add shared MCP lifecycle management with drafts, review, publish, online/offline operations, visibility, Java SDKs, and historical reconciliation while preserving existing Config/Naming serving data.

## Enhancement/Refactor

- [#8354](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/8354) Replace the mandatory Prometheus client dependency with a pluggable client metrics SPI and a no-op default.
- [#12064](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/12064) Support configuring the gRPC port offset through individual client properties.
- [#12734](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/12734) Add request/result-based Config SDK methods, encrypted Config CAS publishing, and conditional queries with local cache reuse.
- [#13690](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/13690) Log the resolved client logging configuration and include namespace IDs in subscription logs.
- [#14804](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14804) Improve Agent Console workflows, expose SDK discovery capabilities and A2A conversion helpers, and trace discovery request origins.
- [#14817](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14817) Disable selected deprecated Pipeline and MCP import APIs by default and provide a shared temporary compatibility switch.
- [#14932](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14932) Reduce read-path contention and improve index consistency in the legacy MCP cache.
- [#14980](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14980) Support deregistering persistent Naming instances from Console v3.
- [#15315](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15315)[#15561](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15561) Improve Skill upload precheck, conflict handling, and server-side ZIP validation.
- [#15322](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15322) Remove obsolete Config migration compatibility code and retain only the current Config storage model.
- [#15345](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15345) Return cached Skill frontmatter in list and metadata-detail responses.
- [#15346](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15346) Manage the reserved `latest` label for AI resources on the server.
- [#15357](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15357) Enable Client API authentication by default and validate standard integration scenarios with authentication enabled.
- [#15432](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15432)[#15440](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15440)[#15441](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15441) Remove reviewed unused Java code while preserving required compatibility contracts.
- [#15448](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15448) Improve English translations in Console UI Next.
- [#15486](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15486) Include the Skill owner in upload permission-denied messages.
- [#15606](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15606) Return a stable per-item result for every Skill batch upload candidate.
- [#15661](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15661) Restrict distributed embedded database query results to supported scalar types and registered row mappers.
- [#15678](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15678) Decouple the visibility plugin SPI from server runtime modules.
- [#15686](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15686)[#15692](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15692) Align authorization method resolution with Spring MVC routing and expand controller-level authorization regression coverage.
- [#15687](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15687) Authenticate native JRaft gRPC requests with server identity and a rolling-upgrade enforcement transition.
- [#15695](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15695) Improve Config detail, edit, and history page layouts with larger content areas and full-screen reading.
- [#15720](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15720) Automatically publish the first uploaded Skill version.
- [#15746](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15746) Add operator-controlled outbound access policies for MCP tool imports.
- [#15837](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15837) Add opt-in initialization for multiple Spring AOT contexts and improve GraalVM runtime metadata.
- [#15838](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15838) Clarify that rolling back the first inserted Config history record deletes the configuration.
- [#15854](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15854) Remove untagged legacy Raft request parsing and preserve explicit errors for malformed log entries.
- [#15868](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15868) Support disabling local Config snapshots through the `configSnapshotEnabled` startup property.
- [#15896](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15896) Migrate Copilot streaming to typed AgentScope events while preserving the existing SSE response contract.
- [#15900](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15900) Correlate Java SDK HTTP requests with server request context through `Nacos-Request-Id`.
- [#15903](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15903) Add a runnable Parallel Search MCP example for registration, endpoint discovery, web search, and page fetching.
- [#15921](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15921) Add optional Jev relevance filtering for ARD Search, with stable result ordering and fallback to basic search.
- [#15929](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15929) Add Russian localization and a language selector to Console UI Next.
- [#15956](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15956) Allow visibility plugins to declare additional AI resource scopes and extend Agent validation through an optional SPI, while preserving default PUBLIC/PRIVATE behavior.

## BugFix

- [#11122](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/11122) Accept `healthCheckEnabled` as a health-check switch entry while retaining the legacy `check` alias.
- [#11780](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/11780) Preserve Config and service list filters and pagination when returning from detail pages.
- [#11890](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/11890) Avoid removing metadata for instances that still exist after restart.
- [#12557](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/12557) Retry Config dump write-lock acquisition to prevent stale MD5 cache data.
- [#14008](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14008) Fix native-image metadata required to establish gRPC client connections.
- [#14804](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14804) Keep AI search available with partial results while indexes are being backfilled.
- [#14804](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14804) Preserve Agent SDK Watches across transient failures and deliver initial and updated state through a consistent Listener path.
- [#14981](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14981)[#15468](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15468) Fix concurrent Config publish duplicate-key handling through the datasource dialect SPI, including PostgreSQL `unique_violation`.
- [#15410](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15410) Fix trailing separators when joining collections containing null elements.
- [#15415](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15415) Prevent malformed config-plugin property names from discarding valid plugin configuration.
- [#15420](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15420) Fix Skill ZIP uploads with invalid or unavailable version candidates.
- [#15425](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15425) Prevent out-of-range batch indexes from causing `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
- [#15446](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15446) Fix page count calculation for empty and exactly divisible result sets.
- [#15447](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15447) Prevent `NamingUtils.getServiceName` from failing on a trailing service separator.
- [#15466](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15466) Correct `@Since` annotations for Skill upload APIs.
- [#15470](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15470) Prevent Naming connection cleanup from waiting for unrelated distributed-lock Raft writes.
- [#15475](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15475) Fix standalone Console auth plugin initialization and forward the caller identity to downstream Server requests.
- [#15476](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15476) Enforce Prompt visibility on list, detail, version, download, and Client read APIs.
- [#15477](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15477) Wait for persistent service metadata before starting health checks.
- [#15490](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15490) Fix Chinese text corruption in Skill Scanner pipeline reports on Windows.
- [#15494](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15494) Restore complete MCP tool advanced-template support in Console UI Next.
- [#15510](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15510) Reject explicitly supplied invalid Bearer tokens instead of falling back to anonymous access.
- [#15534](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15534) Generate deterministic, ASCII-safe physical Config keys for AI resources.
- [#15543](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15543) Restore case-sensitive collation for newly initialized MySQL Config schemas.
- [#15557](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15557) Fix startup failures when plugin state snapshots are restored before unified plugin discovery.
- [#15560](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15560) Preserve MCP tool passthrough authentication when editing and publishing runtime templates.
- [#15603](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15603) Fix visibility query conversion when explicitly authorized resources are present.
- [#15618](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15618) Try lower-priority explicit Skill upload versions before generating a version.
- [#15620](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15620) Allow AI resource versions to be resubmitted after completed or stale review results.
- [#15625](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15625) Fix gray Config cache null access and cross-thread visibility in Config disk services and client connections.
- [#15634](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15634) Fix API authorization metadata, custom resource parser precedence, AgentSpec authorization, and Prometheus security path matching.
- [#15642](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15642) Make AI resource deletion cleanup-first and retryable across all stored versions.
- [#15658](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15658) Keep AI resource reads, updates, and deletion bound to the persisted storage provider.
- [#15660](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15660) Fix standalone Console startup when the Config clone source-permission checker is unavailable.
- [#15663](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15663) Preserve case-sensitive AI resource identities in MySQL search and task tables.
- [#15675](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15675) Preserve nullable MCP tool output schemas during editing, display, and OpenAPI import.
- [#15682](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15682) Prevent login responses from disclosing whether a username exists.
- [#15689](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15689) Preserve string serialization of Config storage IDs with Jackson 3 to avoid numeric precision loss.
- [#15701](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15701) Fix Config history next-record queries on Derby and preserve gray-version filtering.
- [#15703](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15703) Migrate the legacy skills.sh importer state key without overriding canonical configuration.
- [#15705](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15705) Clean removed Skill and AgentSpec draft files while retaining retry metadata after storage failures.
- [#15710](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15710) Declare the required SQL LIKE escape clause for Derby, Oracle, and other affected dialects.
- [#15712](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15712)[#15827](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15827) Reject unsafe instance addresses, HTTP targets, headers, and MySQL connection options in active health checks.
- [#15714](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15714) Handle encoded context paths consistently in the legacy controller-method resolver.
- [#15718](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15718) Escape all LIKE predicates when searching embedded roles with username filters.
- [#15724](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15724) Forward the namespace when querying Config listeners by IP across cluster members.
- [#15744](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15744) Align bootstrap and distribution configuration defaults.
- [#15763](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15763) Reject invalid IPv6 mixed addresses with too many explicit address blocks.
- [#15788](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15788) Allow the Java client to run with Jackson 3 after excluding Jackson 2 core/databind, including authentication paths.
- [#15803](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15803) Reject unsafe AgentSpec and Skill ZIP layouts and enforce entry-count and decompression limits.
- [#15804](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15804) Reject unsafe filesystem paths before Config, archive, and local rule-storage operations.
- [#15821](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15821) Increase the embedded Derby connection timeout to prevent initialization failures on slow storage.
- [#15836](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15836) Fix plugin availability RPC serialization so remote cluster members are reported correctly.
- [#15844](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15844) Use the correct default gRPC protocol negotiator type.
- [#15847](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15847) Restore public defaults for newly created Agent and MCP resources and preserve existing visibility scopes.
- [#15850](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15850)[#15851](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15851) Select the default JDBC driver from the datasource dialect and clarify non-MySQL configuration examples.
- [#15853](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15853) Return schema metadata in current, historical, and previous-version Config details.
- [#15857](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15857) Prevent stale Distro snapshots from overwriting redo registrations and losing service instances after cluster restarts.
- [#15864](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15864) Resolve HEAD requests through their GET mapping in the legacy controller-method cache.
- [#15866](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15866) Remove server-list event subscriptions on client shutdown and prevent callbacks from accessing a closed server-list provider.
- [#15872](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15872) Display subscriber addresses, client versions, and application names correctly in Console UI Next.
- [#15876](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15876) Ignore registration responses from obsolete connections so ephemeral instances are re-registered after reconnect storms.
- [#15883](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15883) Fix unexpected HTTP 403 responses from identity-only APIs when Console is deployed independently.
- [#15899](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15899) Fix Console UI Next loading failures on Chromium 90 by transpiling unsupported JavaScript syntax.
- [#15930](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15930) Prevent uncaught errors from permanently cancelling Naming redo tasks and blocking registration or subscription recovery.
- [#15945](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15945)[#15947](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15947) Parse multiline YAML Skill descriptions correctly and prevent spurious frontmatter fields.
- [#15946](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15946) Preserve empty and whitespace-only Skill resource files when reading versions and downloading packages.
- [#15949](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15949) Keep Skill descriptions consistent with the displayed version across draft edits and lifecycle transitions, and retain the correct description when the last online version goes offline.
- [#15953](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15953) Keep Publish and Cancel actions visible on Config creation and edit pages, and eliminate nested scrolling on Config and history detail pages in Console UI Next.

## Dependencies

- [#14944](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/14944) Upgrade Spring Boot from 3.5.14 to 4.0.6.
- [#15470](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15470) Upgrade SOFA JRaft to 1.4.1 while preserving callback cache behavior and JRaft authentication.
- [#15584](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15584) Upgrade Maven Compiler Plugin from 3.5.1 to 3.15.0 for JDK 25 build compatibility.
- [#15645](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15645)[#15834](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15834)[#15944](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15944) Update legacy and next Console dependencies, refresh packaged assets, and upgrade the bundled DOMPurify sanitizer to 3.4.17.
- [#15707](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/pull/15707) Upgrade Log4j API from 2.25.4 to 2.25.5.
- [#15767](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15767) Upgrade gRPC to 1.81.0 to address CVE-2026-33871.
- [#15796](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15796) Upgrade Apache Derby from 10.14.2.0 to 10.16.1.1, align split artifacts, and retain the Java 17 baseline.
- [#15878](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/issues/15878) Upgrade AgentScope Java from 1.0.7 to 2.0.3 in Copilot.

---

## Breaking Change Notice

Nacos 3.3.0 changes authentication defaults, disables selected deprecated APIs, and introduces migration requirements. Applications using the new Agent SDK from BETA or RC also need to review the finalized subscription contract.

Affected users:

- Applications relying on Client APIs without credentials or on deprecated Pipeline and MCP import endpoints.
- Deployments with legacy Config data, historical AI storage keys, untagged Raft logs, or A2A/MCP resources requiring migration.
- Applications relying on built-in Prometheus client metrics or implicit AI resource visibility defaults.
- BETA/RC adopters using RAD subscriptions or remotely accessing the optional DNS server.

Recommended upgrade path:

- **Prepare Client API credentials.** An absent `nacos.core.auth.enabled` now means `true`. Existing explicit `false` settings remain effective. If necessary, keep authentication explicitly disabled during credential provisioning, then enable it consistently across the cluster after verifying client access. Admin and Console authentication defaults are unchanged.
- **Migrate deprecated AI API calls.** Selected legacy Pipeline and Console MCP import endpoints return HTTP `410` with `API_DEPRECATED` by default. Use the Pipeline `/list` and `/detail` endpoints and unified `/v3/console/ai/import/validate` and `/execute` endpoints. `nacos.core.api.compatibility.enabled=true` temporarily reopens the selected endpoints; `nacos.ai.resource.import.legacy-mcp-api-enabled` is no longer recognized.
- **Complete legacy Config migrations.** Upgrade pre-3.0 deployments through an earlier Nacos 3.x version. Migrate default-namespace data from the empty tenant to `public`, and legacy beta/tag data to `config_info_gray`. For the `nacos_config` AI storage provider, explicitly migrate affected historical non-ASCII or overlength Config coordinates to the deterministic ASCII-safe mapping.
- **Check persisted Raft logs.** Nacos 3.3 no longer replays untagged entries, including entries originally written by Nacos 2.0.x and retained through intermediate upgrades. Recover and migrate those logs or snapshots with a compatible version before upgrading; changing the running version alone does not convert persisted logs.
- **Plan historical A2A and MCP migration.** The default `nacos.ai.a2a.compatibility.mode=CANONICAL` does not scan historical A2A data. Follow the [A2A upgrade runbook](https://github.com/alibaba/nacos/blob/043954fdf52bceaf1be2d14b04072010220ceed3/specs/en/ai/a2a-upgrade-migration-spec.md#9-upgrade-runbook) for `AUTO` migration and early-3.3 preflight. After permanent canonical cutover, legacy-only servers must not rejoin. Preserve MCP reconciliation state and its existing Config/Naming serving data during the one-way lifecycle transition.
- **Keep cluster server identities consistent.** Native JRaft authentication becomes enforced after all members advertise support, and enforcement persists across restarts. Rolling downgrades to members without JRaft credential support are not guaranteed to remain available.
- **Update BETA/RC Agent SDK consumers.** The new RAD `subscribeAgent` methods now return `void`. Receive both initial state and subsequent updates through the Listener, prepare Listener state before subscribing, and recompile dependent applications. Legacy A2A signatures and HTTP/gRPC wire contracts remain unchanged.
- **Configure client metrics explicitly.** `nacos-client` no longer includes a mandatory Prometheus client dependency. Install an implementation of `NacosClientMetricsProvider` when metrics are required; without one, recording is a no-op even when `enableClientMetrics` is enabled.
- **Review MCP import and visibility settings.** Private or local MCP import targets require `nacos.console.ai.mcp.import.allowed-private-addresses`, and redirects are not followed. The built-in visibility plugin defaults newly created Agent and MCP resources to `PUBLIC`; explicitly choose a private scope where required. Existing stored scopes and Prompt/Skill defaults are unchanged.
- **Review DNS listener configuration.** DNS remains optional and disabled by default. When enabled, `nacos.naming.dns.bind-address` defaults to `127.0.0.1`; configure the intended listening address for remote clients. External forwarding requires separate explicit configuration.
- **Refresh affected Skill metadata.** Historical Skill descriptors without parsed frontmatter retain their existing metadata; this release does not automatically read their packages or backfill missing metadata. Update the content or re-upload affected Skills to regenerate frontmatter and correct previously stored multiline descriptions.
- **Back up and rehearse the upgrade.** Back up the database and persisted server data, then verify authentication, data migration, discovery, and client behavior in staging. Embedded Derby is upgraded to 10.16.1.1, so include persisted-data reads, subsequent writes, and restart recovery in upgrade validation.

Deployments without the affected historical data do not require those data migrations. The authentication defaults and any applicable API or SDK changes still need review.

---

## Java Version Requirements

| Module | Java Required |
|--------|--------------|
| Nacos-Server / Nacos-Console | Java 17 |
| Nacos-Client | Java 8 |
| Nacos-Maintainer-Client | Java 8 |

---

data.name: BFE v1.8.9.1
data.body:
### Added
- Add `Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding` (`auto`/`identity`/`off`, default `auto`): how `Accept-Encoding` is rewritten on an AI upstream request, so content negotiation stays inside the coding set the gateway can decode (`gzip`, `deflate`). `auto` keeps only the decodable codings of the client's list (q values preserved, an empty intersection is left untouched, `identity;q=0` is honoured), `identity` strips compression for diagnostics, `off` keeps the previous behaviour. The rewrite only touches the outbound header: the inbound request, the access log, `mod_ai_cache` and `mod_compress` still see the client value (issue #1468)
- Add `bfe_util.NewContentDecoder` / `CanDecodeContentEncoding` / `SupportedContentEncodings`, a streaming `Content-Encoding` decoder covering `gzip`/`x-gzip` and `deflate` (zlib header sniffed, raw DEFLATE accepted). `DecodeContentEncoding` now delegates to it, so the non-streaming parse-only copy also understands `deflate` (issue #1468)
- Add the `ResStreamCompressed` / `ResStreamDecoded` / `ResStreamDecodeSkipped` / `ResStreamRawOnly` `mod_body_process` counters: how many responses carried a `Content-Encoding`, how many got the decompress-for-parsing tap, how many could not be decoded and how many degraded mid-stream. The last two mean "this request is billed by estimation", i.e. the only signal that an upstream ignored the narrowed `Accept-Encoding` (issue #1468)

### Changed
- An AI upstream request whose client `Accept-Encoding` contains codings the gateway cannot decode no longer receives them (`Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding = auto`, the default): the upstream is offered `gzip`/`deflate` only, so a client that asked for `zstd` may now receive `gzip` instead (still inside its own `Accept-Encoding`, <1% size difference). Set `Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding = off` to keep the previous negotiation (issue #1468)

### Fixed
- Parse the usage of a compressed streaming (SSE) response instead of estimating it: `mod_body_process` bypassed any `Content-Encoding` body to a byte-wise pass-through, so `cache_read_tokens` stayed 0, `prompt_tokens` fell back to the request-body estimate and `completion_tokens` to the compressed-bytes estimate, and the whole prompt was billed at the input price — measured on the field at a 96% cache-hit rate that overcharges by roughly 46x and writes `ai_usage_source=estimated`. Compressed SSE now goes through `CompressedStreamDecoder`, which tees the source into a decompressor used only for parsing while the original compressed bytes are forwarded verbatim together with the `Content-Encoding` header; a decompression failure or an unsupported coding degrades to a byte-exact pass-through plus the estimate, visibly (issue #1468)
- Report a skipped `stream_options.include_usage` injection when the request body exceeds `Server.AccessibleBodySize`: the injection used to fail silently, which raised the probability of an upstream returning no usage at all (issue #1468)

```shell
kubectl apply -f https://infra.tekton.dev/tekton-releases/pipeline/previous/v1.18.0/release.yaml
```

## Attestation

The Rekor UUID for this release is `108e9186e8c5677a60b5706509f09f5e185c25597018b15d790c34d2a4f4357d357cb747b9fe0109`

Obtain the attestation:
```shell
REKOR_UUID=108e9186e8c5677a60b5706509f09f5e185c25597018b15d790c34d2a4f4357d357cb747b9fe0109
rekor-cli get --uuid $REKOR_UUID --format json | jq -r .Attestation | jq .
```

Verify that all container images in the attestation are in the release file:
```shell
RELEASE_FILE=https://infra.tekton.dev/tekton-releases/pipeline/previous/v1.18.0/release.yaml
REKOR_UUID=108e9186e8c5677a60b5706509f09f5e185c25597018b15d790c34d2a4f4357d357cb747b9fe0109

# Obtains the list of images with sha from the attestation
REKOR_ATTESTATION_IMAGES=$(rekor-cli get --uuid "$REKOR_UUID" --format json | jq -r .Attestation | jq -r '.subject[]|.name + ":v1.18.0@sha256:" + .digest.sha256')

# Download the release file
curl -L "$RELEASE_FILE" > release.yaml

# For each image in the attestation, match it to the release file
for image in $REKOR_ATTESTATION_IMAGES; do
  printf $image; grep -q $image release.yaml && echo " ===> ok" || echo " ===> no match";
done
```

For installation guides, please check out [play.etcd.io](http://play.etcd.io) and [operating etcd](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/op-guide/). Latest support status for common architectures and operating systems can be found at [supported platforms](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/op-guide/supported-platform/).

###### Linux

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

# choose either URL
GOOGLE_URL=https://storage.googleapis.com/etcd
GITHUB_URL=https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/download
DOWNLOAD_URL=${GOOGLE_URL}

rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz
rm -rf /tmp/etcd-download-test && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-download-test

curl -L ${DOWNLOAD_URL}/${ETCD_VER}/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz -o /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar xzvf /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz -C /tmp/etcd-download-test --strip-components=1 --no-same-owner
rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz

/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd --version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdutl version

# start a local etcd server
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd

# write,read to etcd
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl --endpoints=localhost:2379 put foo bar
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl --endpoints=localhost:2379 get foo
```

###### macOS (Darwin)

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

# choose either URL
GOOGLE_URL=https://storage.googleapis.com/etcd
GITHUB_URL=https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/download
DOWNLOAD_URL=${GOOGLE_URL}

rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
rm -rf /tmp/etcd-download-test && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-download-test

curl -L ${DOWNLOAD_URL}/${ETCD_VER}/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip -o /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
unzip /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip -d /tmp && rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
mv /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64/* /tmp/etcd-download-test && rm -rf mv /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64

/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd --version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdutl version
```

###### Docker

etcd uses [`gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd`](https://gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd) as a primary container registry, and [`quay.io/coreos/etcd`](https://quay.io/coreos/etcd) as secondary.

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

rm -rf /tmp/etcd-data.tmp && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-data.tmp && \
  docker rmi gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:${ETCD_VER} || true && \
  docker run \
  -p 2379:2379 \
  -p 2380:2380 \
  --mount type=bind,source=/tmp/etcd-data.tmp,destination=/etcd-data \
  --name etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} \
  gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:${ETCD_VER} \
  /usr/local/bin/etcd \
  --name s1 \
  --data-dir /etcd-data \
  --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 \
  --advertise-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 \
  --listen-peer-urls http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-advertise-peer-urls http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-cluster s1=http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-cluster-token tkn \
  --initial-cluster-state new \
  --log-level info \
  --logger zap \
  --log-outputs stderr

docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcd --version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdutl version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl endpoint health
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl put foo bar
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl get foo
```

# Quick Start

## What's New?

Find out on [our blog](https://blog.argoproj.io) and [changelog](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Check the [upgrading guide](https://argo-workflows.readthedocs.io/en/latest/upgrading/) and search for [existing issues on GitHub](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/issues).

## Installation

### CLI

#### Mac / Linux

Available via `curl`

```bash
# Detect OS
ARGO_OS="darwin"
if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]]; then
  ARGO_OS="linux"
fi

# Download the binary
curl -sLO "https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/releases/download/v4.1.6/argo-$ARGO_OS-amd64.gz"

# Unzip
gunzip "argo-$ARGO_OS-amd64.gz"

# Make binary executable
chmod +x "argo-$ARGO_OS-amd64"

# Move binary to path
mv "./argo-$ARGO_OS-amd64" /usr/local/bin/argo

# Test installation
argo version
```

### Controller and Server

```bash
kubectl create namespace argo
kubectl apply -n argo -f https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/releases/download/v4.1.6/install.yaml
```

data.name: Release 2.45.3 LTS
data.body:
## Known issues

- On Async Edge environments, an invalid update schedule date can be displayed when browsing a snapshot

### Known issues with Podman support

- Podman environments aren't supported by auto-onboarding script
- It's not possible to add Podman environments via socket, when running a Portainer server on Docker (and vice versa)
- Support for only CentOS 9, Podman 5 rootful

## Changes

### Breaking changes

- Portainer no longer trusts TLS certificates issued by eMudhra (emSign), following the compromise of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943). Connections to services that present an affected certificate, including OAuth/OIDC and LDAPS providers, registries and Git hosts, will fail after the upgrade. If your single sign-on or LDAP provider is affected, only the initial admin will be able to sign in. Check your services before upgrading. [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)

### Security improvements

- Rejected Compose and Swarm stacks using `volumes_from` when non-administrators create, update, start or redeploy them with `Hide bind mounts for non-administrators` enabled, which let them inherit another container's host bind mounts
- Updated the Go toolchain to 1.26.10, fixing CVE-2026-56857 and CVE-2026-78663 (both Critical), along with CVE-2026-111943, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97031, CVE-2026-94440, CVE-2026-94439, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-56866, CVE-2026-94448 and CVE-2026-97030
- Removed the eMudhra emSign root certificates from the CA bundle in Linux images, and rejected certificate chains that contain the compromised eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943). [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)
- Updated [golang.org/x/net](http://golang.org/x/net) to 0.60.0, fixing CVE-2026-78663 (Critical), CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78660 and CVE-2026-78659 (all High)
- Updated helm in the kubectl shell image to v4.3.1, taking its Go toolchain to 1.27.2 and oras.land/oras-go/v2 to 2.6.2, fixing CVE-2026-39821 (Critical) and CVE-2026-50163 (High)
- Restricted kubeconfig tokens to the /api/endpoints/{id}/kubernetes proxy, so they are rejected with a 403 on every other API route, including admin-only routes and the Docker proxy. Kubeconfigs downloaded after upgrading carry a separate token per environment, limited to that environment 

### Bug fixes

- Fixed starting a container with an empty request body failing with a 400 error on Docker standalone and Swarm agent environments 
- Fixed GitOps sources starting a new poll while the previous one was still running, which could pile up overlapping redeploys on slow repositories. A poll that is still running now causes the next scheduled poll to be skipped
- Fixed GitOps workflows showing the Git reference and file path status as unknown after a stack was manually redeployed from Git. A manual redeploy now records these statuses for the stack's workflow artifact
- Fixed the YAML tab on the Kubernetes node details page going blank after switching tabs or refocusing the browser, and restored the missing gap between the tab content and the Applications table
- Fixed DockerHub pull rate limits and agent version detection failing on Docker engines newer than API 1.47, and, in BE, non-admin users with environment access getting 403 errors on `/agent/docker` and `/agent/host` routes, which left Swarm node selectors empty
- Fixed the search box on the Authentication logs page not filtering events by username

## Deprecated and removed features

None.
